opening.text: A slow-cooked meal tastes better than a fast one. You cannot rush it. The flavor needs time.
Pondering is slow cooking for the soul. We take a truth and let it sit. Here is why that is worth doing.

mainMessage.text: To ponder is to think deeply and pray about what we have read or learned. It is not a quick task. Truth comes in small pieces. As we ponder, God teaches us. We keep a record, and we draw near to Him.

blocks.text: Slow down.
Mary kept the things she heard about her son and thought about them in her heart. Proverbs says to ponder the path of our feet.
But Mary kept all these things, and pondered them in her heart.
Ponder the path of thy feet, and let all thy ways be established.
Elder Richard G. Scott of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Acquiring Spiritual Knowledge” from the October 1993 general conference.
Prayerful reflection yields further understanding.
Good things need time.
Let it simmer overnight.
The Savior told the people to go home and ponder His words. They were to ask the Father and prepare for the next day.

I perceive that ye are weak, that ye cannot understand all my words which I am commanded of the Father to speak unto you at this time. Therefore, go ye unto your homes, and ponder upon the things which I have said, and ask of the Father, in my name, that ye may understand, and prepare your minds for the morrow, and I come unto you again.
Draw near unto me and I will draw near unto you; seek me diligently and ye shall find me; ask, and ye shall receive; knock, and it shall be opened unto you.
Elder Richard G. Scott of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Acquiring Spiritual Knowledge” from the October 1993 general conference.
Precious truth comes a small piece at a time through faith, with great exertion, and at times wrenching struggles.
Not every truth is quick.
Add a question.
Nephi pondered as he walked home. Alma said we can test the word by giving it a chance to work in us.
And it came to pass that Nephi went his way towards his own house, pondering upon the things which the Lord had shown unto him.

But behold, if ye will awake and arouse your faculties, even to an experiment upon my words, and exercise a particle of faith, yea, even if ye can no more than desire to believe, let this desire work in you, even until ye believe in a manner that ye can give place for a portion of my words.
Elder Richard G. Scott of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Acquiring Spiritual Knowledge” from the October 1993 general conference.
Gaining spiritual knowledge is not a mechanical process.
It takes a real heart.
Ponder the mercy of the Lord.
Moroni asked us to remember how merciful the Lord has been and ponder it in our hearts. Joseph Smith and Sidney Rigdon pondered, and the Lord opened their understanding.

Behold, I would exhort you that when ye shall read these things, if it be wisdom in God that ye should read them, that ye would remember how merciful the Lord hath been unto the children of men, from the creation of Adam even down until the time that ye shall receive these things, and ponder it in your hearts.
And while we meditated upon these things, the Lord touched the eyes of our understandings and they were opened, and the glory of the Lord shone round about.
Elder Richard G. Scott of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Acquiring Spiritual Knowledge” from the October 1993 general conference.
Profound spiritual truth cannot simply be poured from one mind and heart to another.
We each have to take it in for ourselves.
Write it down.
Nephi said his heart pondered continually on what he had seen and heard. Joshua was told to think on God’s law day and night.
Behold, my soul delighteth in the things of the Lord; and my heart pondereth continually upon the things which I have seen and heard.

This book of the law shall not depart out of thy mouth; but thou shalt meditate therein day and night, that thou mayest observe to do according to all that is written therein: for then thou shalt make thy way prosperous, and then thou shalt have good success.
Elder Richard G. Scott of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Acquiring Spiritual Knowledge” from the October 1993 general conference.
Knowledge carefully recorded is knowledge available in time of need.
What we write, we keep.
Talk to Him about it.
The psalmist meditated on God’s precepts. Alma fasted and prayed for many days, and then he knew.
I will meditate in thy precepts, and have respect unto thy ways.

Behold, I say unto you they are made known unto me by the Holy Spirit of God. Behold, I have fasted and prayed many days that I might know these things of myself. And now I do know of myself that they are true; for the Lord God hath made them manifest unto me by his Holy Spirit; and this is the spirit of revelation which is in me.
President Russell M. Nelson, President of the Church, said this in his talk “Revelation for the Church, Revelation for Our Lives” from the April 2018 general conference.
Pray in the name of Jesus Christ about your concerns, your fears, your weaknesses.
Pondering and prayer go hand in hand.

blocks.text: King Benjamin taught his people about what goes on in the mind.

But this much I can tell you, that if ye do not watch yourselves, and your thoughts, and your words, and your deeds, and observe the commandments of God, and continue in the faith of what ye have heard concerning the coming of our Lord, even unto the end of your lives, ye must perish.
